10.1002_smll.76678: The shuttle effect of soluble polyiodides limits the cycling stability and rate capability of aqueous Zn‐I 2 batteries. Herein, a ZrO 2 ‐decorated cellulose‐derived carbon aerogel (ZCA) is developed by integrating hierarchical pore confinement with polarized Zr─O/carbon interfacial regulation. Spectroscopic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal moderate O···I─I coupling with halogen‐bond‐like character for neutral I 2 at Zr‐adjacent oxygen sites, while reduced iodine species are stabilized through species‐dependent interfacial regulation within the polarized Zr─O‐containing environment. This structural‐interfacial synergy suppresses polyiodide diffusion while preserving reversible I − /I 3 − /I 2 conversion. Consequently, ZCA@I 2 delivers 187.2 mAh g −1 after 5000 cycles at 1 A g −1 and sustains 123.2 mAh g −1 after 50 000 cycles at 10 A g −1 , with a per‐cycle decay of only 0.000052%. At an iodine areal loading of 6.7 mg cm −2 , it retains 93.1% of its capacity after 6000 cycles at 1 A g −1 . These results provide a structure‐interface design strategy for durable, high‐rate, and high‐loading aqueous Zn‐I 2 batteries.
10.1002_smsc.70414: The use of solid electrolytes (SEs) allows for the construction of solid‐state cells with bilayer‐to‐multilayer architectures. By appropriate choice of electrolytes for the positive‐ and negative‐electrode sides, electrolyte degradation can be mitigated, thus considerably increasing the design flexibility. However, certain electrolyte combinations lead to nonideal chemical compatibility, increasing the heteroelectrolyte interfacial resistance. Precise measurement of the interfacial resistance is necessary for quantitatively evaluating the compatibility of solid electrolytes. In this work, we employed a solid‐state four‐electrode cell to investigate the compatibility between three chloride‐based SEs—(Li 3 InCl 6 (LIC), Li 3 ScCl 6 (LSC), and Li 3 YCl 6 (LYC))—and the sulfide‐based Li 7 P 2 S 8 I (LPSI). Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis reveals that the growth rate of the interfacial resistance is the highest in LIC, but the activation energies of the interfacial resistances are identical in all three SEs. Temperature‐dependent synchrotron X‐ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations strongly suggest that Li 4 PS 4 I, whose activation energy is similar to those measured by EIS, is the common interfacial product among the three cells, and that its relative degree of formation is consistent with the difference in interfacial resistance growth. This study demonstrates that electrochemical measurements using solid‐state four‐electrode cells constitute a promising technique for precisely investigating unstable heteroelectrolyte interfaces.
10.1021_acsami.6c05058: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) hold great promise for large-scale energy storage, yet their practical application is hindered by Zn dendrites, interfacial corrosion, and sluggish Zn 2+ transportation. Herein, we propose a novel 3D confined zinc storage strategy by constructing a nitrogen-doped hard carbon (N-BHC) coating on the Zn anode. The N-BHC features abundant closed pores and uniformly distributed pyridinic N sites, enabling multisynergistic regulation. Specifically, its framework acts as a physical barrier to isolate Zn from electrolytes, suppressing hydrogen evolution and corrosion. The closed pores are suggested to act as localized Zn 2+ storage reservoirs to homogenize electric field distribution, thereby inhibiting dendrite formation. Moreover, pyridinic N sites enhance ion conductivity, accelerating Zn 2+ transport kinetics. Benefiting from these merits, the N-BHC@Zn anode exhibits exceptional cycling stability (over 2500 h at 1 mA cm –2 /1 mAh cm –2 ), ultralow polarization (∼18 mV) and superior rate capability even at 5 mA cm –2 . Furthermore, the N-BHC@Zn//MnO 2 full cell delivers a specific capacity above 200 mAh g –1 at 1 A g –1 even after 1200 cycles. This work establishes a new paradigm for regulating ion transport and stabilizing electrode–electrolyte interfaces through rational pore structure engineering. This strategy can be readily extended to other aqueous metal-ion batteries that exhibit similar dendrite and corrosion issues.
10.1039_d6ta06659c: This review introduces high-voltage LiCoO 2 degradation mechanisms with stabilization strategies and practical pathways toward durable, sustainable, high-energy Li-ion batteries.
